learn-to-type.name: 小飞机射击
learn-to-type.description: 从基础键位到全键进阶，用游戏闯关模式逐级解锁打字技能，适合零基础与中级用户。每关聚焦特定键区，像玩游戏升段位一样轻松建立指法记忆，练出扎实手感。

learn-to-type.name: 打地鼠
learn-to-type.description: 小时候的经典游戏，可爱的仓鼠你想打吗？那就来玩吧。

learn-to-type.name: 警察抓小偷
learn-to-type.description: 打字追逃游戏！敲对字母警察前进，打错或等待太久小偷就会逃跑。在距离超过限制前追上小偷即可通关！每关练习不同键位，速度逐渐加快，挑战你的反应和打字准确率。

learn-to-type.name: 诗韵打字
learn-to-type.description: 学习经典古诗，同时练习拼音打字。从五言绝句到七言律诗，30首递进式学习，掌握拼音的同时感受诗词之美。

learn-to-type.name: 📖 英文文章练习
learn-to-type.description: 通过经典英文短文练习打字，提升英文输入速度和准确性。从短句到长文章，循序渐进。

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: The cat sits on the mat. It is a small cat. The cat likes to sleep in the sun.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: The dog runs in the park. It is a happy dog. The dog loves to play with a ball.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: I go to school every day. I learn many things. My favorite subject is English. I like to play with my friends.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: There are four people in my family. My father is a doctor. My mother is a teacher. My sister is a student. I love my family very much.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: The sun is very bright. It gives us light and heat. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: I have a pet rabbit. It is white and soft. It likes to eat carrots. I play with it every day.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: The flower is red and beautiful. It smells very good. I water the flower every morning.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Tom is my best friend. He is kind and funny. We play football together. I like to talk with him.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: The bird flies in the sky. It sings a sweet song. The bird lives in a nest in the tree.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: My room is clean and tidy. There is a bed and a desk. I have many books on the shelf. I like my room.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: An old owl lived in an oak tree. Every day he saw many things happening around him. He heard people talking. He noticed that some people were kind and some were not. The owl became wiser every day.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: A hungry fox saw some grapes hanging from a vine. He tried to reach them but could not. He jumped and jumped but still could not reach the grapes. Finally he gave up and said the grapes were sour anyway.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: A boy watched sheep near a village. He cried Wolf to make the villagers come. They came but there was no wolf. He did this many times. One day a wolf really came. The boy cried for help but no one believed him. The wolf ate the sheep.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: A hare laughed at a tortoise for being slow. The tortoise challenged the hare to a race. The hare ran fast and stopped to rest. He fell asleep. The tortoise kept walking slowly. When the hare woke up the tortoise had already won the race.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: A lion caught a little mouse. The mouse asked the lion to let him go. He promised to help the lion one day. The lion laughed but let him go. Later the lion was caught in a net. The mouse chewed the net and set the lion free.

levels.author: Aesop
levels.text: All summer the ant worked hard storing food. The grasshopper played and sang. When winter came the grasshopper had no food. He went to the ant for help. The ant asked what he did all summer. The grasshopper said he sang. The ant told him to dance all winter.

levels.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
levels.text: A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere. Before him I may think aloud. I am arrived at last in the presence of a man who is real. He is the healthiest the most trustworthy the most sensible of men.

levels.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
levels.text: Nature is a sea of forms. It does not repeat itself. Every day the sun rises and sets. Every day the stars shine at night. The beauty of nature fills the heart with joy and peace.

levels.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
levels.text: To laugh often and much to win the respect of intelligent people to earn the appreciation of honest critics to leave the world a bit better whether by a healthy child a garden patch or a redeemed social condition to know even one life has breathed easier because you have lived is to have succeeded.

levels.author: Robert Frost
levels.text: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood. And sorry I could not travel both. And be one traveler long I stood. And looked down one as far as I could. To where it bent in the undergrowth.

levels.author: Robert Frost
levels.text: Whose woods these are I think I know. His house is in the village though. He will not see me stopping here. To watch his woods fill up with snow. The woods are lovely dark and deep. But I have promises to keep. And miles to go before I sleep.

levels.author: Langston Hughes
levels.text: Hold fast to dreams for if dreams die life is a broken winged bird that cannot fly. Hold fast to dreams for when dreams go life is a barren field frozen with snow.

levels.description: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
levels.author: William Wordsworth
levels.text: I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills. When all at once I saw a crowd a host of golden daffodils. Beside the lake beneath the trees fluttering and dancing in the breeze.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Kindness is a simple act that can change someone's day. A smile a hug or a few kind words can make a big difference. Always try to be kind to others. The world needs more kindness.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Life is full of challenges. Sometimes you will fail. But do not give up. Keep trying and you will succeed. Remember that every failure is a step closer to success. Believe in yourself.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Time is more valuable than money. You can earn more money but you cannot get back lost time. Use your time wisely. Do not waste it on things that do not matter. Every moment is precious.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Being grateful for what you have is the key to happiness. Take a moment each day to think about the good things in your life. Family friends health and love are all things to be thankful for.

levels.author: Unknown
levels.text: Reading opens the door to new worlds. It helps you learn new things and see different perspectives. Books can take you on adventures without leaving your home. Make reading a daily habit.

levels.author: Rudyard Kipling
levels.text: If you can keep your head when all about you are losing theirs and blaming it on you. If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you but make allowance for their doubting too. Yours is the earth and everything that's in it. And which is more you'll be a man my son.

levels.author: William Ernest Henley
levels.text: Out of the night that covers me black as the pit from pole to pole. I thank whatever gods may be for my unconquerable soul. In the fell clutch of circumstance I have not winced nor cried aloud. Under the bludgeonings of chance my head is bloody but unbowed. I am the master of my fate. I am the captain of my soul.
